headline: Braga's new coach — still 60.2% favourites at Nacional
summary: Braga go to Nacional on Sunday with a new coach. Carlos Vicens was sacked after the 1-2 home defeat to Gil Vicente, and Franclim Carvalho takes charge for the first time. Nacional are 16th with 4 points and have lost all 5 of their last matches, so the market still makes Braga 60.2% favourites — the average across 10 bookmakers, with the margin removed. The gap in quality is smaller than it was: Braga are rated about a goal better, trimmed from 1.07 to 0.92 goals. Over 2.5 goals is a 50% call.
read: Braga arrive with a new coach and three straight defeats behind them, yet the market still makes them 60% favourites at a Nacional side that has lost five in a row and sits 16th.

facts.fact: Braga sacked head coach Carlos Vicens on 20 October and appointed Franclim Carvalho in his place, with this match his first in charge.
facts.meaning: A new voice in the dressing room, but also four days of upheaval before a league away game.

facts.fact: Braga lost 1-2 at home to Gil Vicente on Sunday, their third defeat in a row.
facts.meaning: Braga arrive on their worst run of the season, having conceded two or more in each of those three games.

facts.fact: Nacional have lost all five of their last matches, the latest a 0-1 exit away to Sanjoanense in the Taça de Portugal.
facts.meaning: The hosts come in with no momentum at all, and they went out of the cup to a side from outside the top flight.

facts.fact: Braga are 60.2% to win at Nacional, who are 16.4% — Braga's chance is nearly four times the home side's.
facts.meaning: The market makes Braga clear favourites despite their three defeats, with the draw at 23.4%.

facts.fact: Braga's win chance has come down from 63.3% to 60.3% in recent days, with Nacional's rising from 14.5% to 16.2%.
facts.meaning: The market has taken some of the certainty out of Braga without abandoning them as favourites.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line has moved from 1.07 to 0.92 goals in Braga's favour.
Nacional are 16th of 18 in the Primeira Liga with four points from eight games.
facts.meaning: The hosts are already in a relegation fight and have little margin for another heavy home defeat.

facts.fact: Nacional created 2.2 xG against Alverca on 12 September but lost 1-3, conceding 1.16 xG.
facts.meaning: Nacional can create at home — the problem has been what they concede and what they take.

sources.fact: SC Braga sacked head coach Carlos Vicens with immediate effect after a disappointing spell in charge.
Franclim Carvalho was officially appointed as SC Braga's new head coach, succeeding Carlos Vicens.
Braga suffered a third consecutive defeat, losing 1-2 at home to Gil Vicente in the Primeira Liga on 19 October.
Braga president António Salvador described the change from Vicens to Carvalho as a cut rather than a transition.
Braga publicly criticised refereeing as a total loss of direction and demanded higher-level intervention, saying they were harmed against Gil Vicente, Moreirense and Sporting.
New Braga coach Franclim Carvalho said he always had the desire to sit in this position.
Braga's António Salvador received a vote of confidence from the SAD amid a period of contestation.
Vicens said in his farewell that it was a privilege to have been part of something so special at Braga.
